At WWDC 2021, Apple announced support for storing driver's licenses in Apple Wallet on iPhone. At the time, Apple marketed this feature as the final step to "completely break free from your physical wallet."

Here are the states where Apple Wallet driver's license support is coming...

Apple Wallet ID Support

In the five years since Apple announced the feature, support has gradually expanded across the United States. Currently, iPhone and Apple Watch users in 14 states and Puerto Rico can add a driver's license or state ID to Apple Wallet. You can see the full list here:

Where will this feature launch next? Here's what we know so far.

The following seven states have confirmed they are working on Apple Wallet driver's license support, been listed by Apple as a partner, or have previously appeared in Apple's code:

  • Kentucky (launching in "summer" 2026)
  • North Carolina (launching in early 2027)
  • Oklahoma (in preparation, no launch date set)
  • Utah (in preparation, no launch date set)
  • Virginia (in preparation, no launch date set)
  • Connecticut (status unknown, previously listed by Apple as a partner)
  • Mississippi (status unknown, previously listed by Apple as a partner)

Meanwhile, the Secure Technology Alliance has been tracking the rollout of mobile driver's licenses across the U.S. Here are some states that have begun exploring mobile ID support through legislation or research, but have not been mentioned by Apple:

  • Indiana
  • Vermont
  • New Jersey
  • Florida
  • South Carolina
  • Tennessee
  • Missouri
  • Nevada
  • Wyoming

It's worth noting that progress varies significantly from state to state. Even if a state is exploring or developing digital ID support, it doesn't necessarily mean it will ultimately launch, nor does it mean it will support Apple Wallet.

Summary

As you can see, the rollout of Apple Wallet driver's license support across the United States remains quite fragmented.

However, you don't have to wait for your state to support Apple Wallet's digital ID feature to try it out.

Apple launched a new digital ID feature last year powered by U.S. passports. Although it's not your driver's license, you can use it at TSA checkpoints at more than 250 airports across the United States with your iPhone.

Have you stored your ID or driver's license in Apple Wallet on your iPhone? Have you actually used it? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
